top_signals.title: The Double Alignment Problem: Civil-Military Relations in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
top_signals.summary:
Artificial intelligence poses the greatest challenge to American civil-military relations since the advent of the nuclear bomb. AI plays outside the political bounds that contain other challenges, however odious. It compounds the inherent problem of civil-military relations – aligning the state and the military – with an additional alignment problem: that of human and agent. In doing so, AI threatens to undermine the constitutionalism and professionalism on which status quo civil-military relations depend. top_signals.title: Battlefield Power Is Running Short
top_signals.summary:
Drones, counter-drone systems, electronic warfare, and edge computing all run on power. Soldiers need more of it, in more places, farther from their supply lines than ever before. How will the Army get it to them? Alex Miller (U.S. Army), Ben Kesling (Chariot Defense), Julie Bush (Valinor Enterprises), and Joel Dillon (Booz Allen) join the show. They discuss moving power to the edge, managing the signatures it creates, and the push for common power standards across the services. They also explore how software can help commanders manage energy like ammunition, and what a well-run battalion’s approach to power might look

top_signals.summary: European Commission Press release Strasbourg, 25 Nov 2026 The European Commission today proposed the Quantum Act, a new framework to help turn Europe's quantum research into products and services, strengthen supply chains and prepare Europe's digital systems for post-quantum cryptography.
